## Previously ...

You have:

- A site, or nearly one
- A statement of what success would look like

. . .

Today we turn that sentence into machinery: a measurement plan, a GA4 property,
events, key events and UTM tags.

. . .

**By the end of today your site will be recording data.**

## Learning Outcomes

By the end of this lecture you will be able to:

- Write a measurement plan that connects an objective to a recorded event
- Create and configure a GA4 property
- Define custom events with parameters, and mark key events
- Tag inbound links with UTM parameters consistently

# 1. The Measurement Plan

## Plan Before Tag

The most common failure in marketing analytics is tagging first.

. . .

You end up with 200 events, no idea which matter, and a report nobody reads.

. . .

**The measurement plan is one page. It is written before you touch GA4.**

## The Structure

Each row goes: objective, question, metric, event, parameter.

| Objective | Question | Metric | Event | Parameters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Get enquiries | Are people contacting me? | Enquiries / week | `generate_lead` | `form_location` |
| Show work | Is anyone reading case studies? | Engaged reads | `read_case_study` | `case_id`, `scroll_pct` |
| Reach | Where do visitors come from? | Sessions by channel | (automatic) | `source`, `medium` |

## Working Backwards

The plan is written right to left in practice:

. . .

1. Start with the **decision** you want to support
2. State the **question** that decision turns on
3. Choose the **metric** that answers it
4. Identify the **event** that produces the metric
5. List the **parameters** you need to slice it

. . .

If you cannot get from a proposed event back to a decision, do not implement it.

## Objectives Are Not Metrics

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Not an objective**

- "Increase engagement"
- "Improve the funnel"
- "Grow the brand"

These cannot be recorded, so they cannot be tested.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**An objective**

- "Get 5 enquiries a month from the contact form"
- "Have half of case study visitors reach the bottom of the page"

These name an action, a count and a period.
:::
::::

# 2. Setting Up GA4

## The Object Model

GA4's hierarchy, which is not the same as Universal Analytics:

```
Account
└── Property          <- your site lives here
    └── Data stream   <- one per platform (web, iOS, Android)
        └── Events    <- everything GA4 records is an event
```

. . .

There are no "goals" and no "views". There are events, and some events are
marked as key events.

## Creating the Property

Walk through, live:

1. `analytics.google.com` → Admin → Create property
2. Property name, **reporting time zone (Dublin)**, currency (EUR)
3. Business details, objectives
4. Create a **Web** data stream with your site URL
5. Copy the measurement ID: `G-XXXXXXXXXX`

. . .

**Set the time zone correctly now.** Changing it later does not restate
historical data, and your weekly cohorts in Lecture 13 will be wrong.

## Installing the Tag

The Google tag goes in `<head>`, on every page.

```{.html}
<!-- Google tag (gtag.js) -->
<script async src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-XXXXXXXXXX"></script>
<script>
  window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
  function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
  gtag('js', new Date());
  gtag('config', 'G-XXXXXXXXXX');
</script>
```

. . .

In Quarto, this goes in `_quarto.yml` under `format: html: include-in-header`,
so it is applied to every page from one place.

## Verifying It

Do not assume it worked.

. . .

- **Realtime report**: load your own site, see yourself appear
- **DebugView**: install the GA Debugger extension, watch individual events
- **Tag Assistant**: confirms the tag fires and reports its configuration

. . .

**A tag that fires on the homepage but not on the contact page is the single
most common cause of a "broken funnel" in Lecture 17.** Check every page.

# 3. Events and Parameters

## Automatic Events

GA4 collects some events without configuration:

- `page_view`
- `session_start`, `first_visit`
- `scroll` (90% depth)
- `click` (outbound links)
- `file_download`
- `video_start`, `video_progress`, `video_complete`

. . .

Enhanced measurement covers most of these. **Check which are on** in your data
stream settings, because they are the ones you get for free.

## Custom Events

For anything specific to your site, you send your own:

```{.html}
<button onclick="gtag('event', 'generate_lead', {
    'form_location': 'contact_page',
    'enquiry_type': 'freelance'
});">Send enquiry</button>
```

. . .

The event name is a **verb**. The parameters are the **adjectives** that let you
slice it later.

## Naming Conventions

Decide once, apply everywhere:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Do**

- `snake_case` throughout
- Verb-object: `read_case_study`
- Use GA4's recommended names where one fits (`generate_lead`, `sign_up`,
  `purchase`)
- Parameter names shared across events
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Do not**

- `ContactFormSubmitted`
- `contact-form-submit`
- `button_click_1`
- A different name for the same action on two pages
:::
::::

. . .

**You cannot rename an event retroactively.** Historical data keeps the old name.

## Parameters and Custom Dimensions

A parameter sent with an event is **not** automatically reportable.

. . .

To use `form_location` as a dimension in a report, register it:

Admin → Custom definitions → Create custom dimension → Event-scoped →
Parameter name `form_location`

. . .

Registration is **not retroactive** either. Register before you need it.

## Key Events

What used to be called conversions.

. . .

Admin → Events → toggle **Mark as key event** on the event that represents your
objective.

. . .

Keep it to **one or two**. If everything is a key event, the conversion rate in
every report becomes meaningless, and the funnel in Lecture 17 has no top.

## Limits Worth Knowing

- 500 distinct event names per property
- 25 parameters per event
- 50 event-scoped custom dimensions
- Event names are case-sensitive: `Sign_Up` and `sign_up` are two events

. . .

These are generous. You will not hit them. The case sensitivity will catch you.

# 4. UTM Parameters

## The Problem UTMs Solve

GA4 can see the referring domain. It cannot see:

- Which newsletter the click came from
- Which of your three LinkedIn posts
- Whether a link was in the bio or in a comment

. . .

Unless you tell it, in the URL.

## The Five Parameters

| Parameter | Answers | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `utm_source` | Which platform? | `linkedin` |
| `utm_medium` | Which type? | `social` |
| `utm_campaign` | Which effort? | `portfolio_launch` |
| `utm_content` | Which variant? | `bio_link` |
| `utm_term` | Which keyword? | `data_analyst_dublin` |

. . .

Source, medium and campaign are the ones you will actually use.

## A Tagged URL

```
https://mysite.ie/work/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=portfolio_launch&utm_content=bio_link
```

. . .

Build these with the Campaign URL Builder rather than by hand:

<https://ga-dev-tools.google/campaign-url-builder/>

## Consistency Is the Whole Point

UTM values are **case-sensitive and free text**. GA4 will happily report:

```
LinkedIn / Social
linkedin / social
Linkedin / social
linkedin / Social
```

. . .

as four separate channels.

. . .

**Write your conventions in a spreadsheet before your first campaign.** All
lowercase, no spaces, a fixed vocabulary for medium. This spreadsheet is what
you will join to in Lecture 12.

## What Not to Tag

<!-- Speaker notes: this is the classic self-referral mistake and it will
     appear in student data if not pre-empted. -->

**Never put UTM parameters on internal links.**

. . .

Tagging a link from your own homepage to your own contact page starts a new
session and attributes it to yourself. Your acquisition report then says your
best traffic source is your own site.

. . .

We will find the damage in Lecture 15.

# 5. AI for the Measurement Plan

## What to Delegate Here

TODO: expand with a live demonstration.

Safe and useful:

- Generating the `gtag` snippet for a custom event with parameters
- Reviewing your event names against GA4's recommended names
- Turning your objective into candidate questions and metrics
- Explaining what a GA4 setting does

## What Not to Delegate

**The objective.** An assistant will invent a plausible one, and you will spend
the semester measuring something you do not care about.

. . .

**The decision about what counts as a key event.** That is a commercial
judgement about your own site.

. . .

**Verification.** It cannot see your Realtime report. Only you can confirm the
tag fires on every page.

## A Prompt That Earns Its Place

> "Here is my measurement plan [paste your table]. For each row, tell me whether
> the event I have chosen can actually produce the metric I have named, and flag
> any parameter I will need but have not listed."

. . .

This catches the most expensive error in the whole block: **an event that cannot
answer the question it was created for**, discovered in Lecture 17 when your
funnel has no middle.
